sections.content: How many people are "metal machining setters and setter-operators"?

38,850 people

were counted on the census as "metal machining setters and setter-operators" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Metal machining setters and setter-operators operate machines to drill, cut, mill or otherwise shape metal workpieces.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "metal machining setters and setter-operators" there were more men than women (96% compared with 4%).

This means "metal machining setters and setter-operators" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled metal, electrical and electronic trades".

Men made up 96% and women made up 4% of "metal machining setters and setter-operators"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "metal machining setters and setter-operators" included:

  • taxi and cab drivers and chauffeurs
  • mining and quarry workers and related operatives
  • rail construction and maintenance operatives

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "metal machining setters and setter-operators" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "metal machining setters and setter-operators", 13.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "metal machining setters and setter-operators" was 16 to 19 years.

We can look at who worked as "metal machining setters and setter-operators" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of men than women with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "metal machining setters and setter-operators" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "metal machining setters and setter-operators", 7.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (95.6% compared with 4.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (97.7%) than self-employed (2.3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the West Midlands. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the same region of the West Midlands.
